title: Broad Adsorption of Sepsis-Related Molecules from Whole Blood Using CytoSorb® Beads
author: Maryann C. Gruda
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kurcwv6
materials: For a large volume reservoir (up to 1L)

steps.title: Assemble CytoSorb column housing
steps.instruction: Assemble the column housing and, if applicable, fill the device with CytoSorb polymer beads.

steps.title: Prepare saline IV bag
steps.instruction: Cut off the bag spike of a 0.9 % saline IV bag, fix the cut tubing with a hose clamp, attach a 3/32 in female Luer fitting to the tubing end, and fill the bag with at least 500 mL saline.

steps.title: Prepare blood filter tubing
steps.instruction: Remove the blood filter from its packaging, cut the tubing 6 in from the filter outlet, position a clamp within 6 in of the outlet, close the clamp, insert the filter spike into the saline bag outlet port, and hang the saline bag on a three‑pronged clamp attached to a ring stand.

steps.title: Attach Luer fitting to filter outlet
steps.instruction: Attach a male 3/32 in Luer fitting to the blood filter outlet tubing.

steps.title: Connect peristaltic tubing to filter
steps.instruction: Attach the red male Luer fitting on the peristaltic tubing to the female Luer fitting on the blood filter, then cut off the red fitting on the opposite end of the peristaltic tubing as close to the fitting as possible.

steps.title: Prepare blood lines tubing
steps.instruction: Remove blood lines from packaging, cut the tubing 12 in short of the in‑line sample port, place a female 5/32 in Luer fitting into the cut end, and connect it to the male 3/32 in Luer fitting on the blood filter tubing; cut off the red fitting on the opposite end of this tubing as close to the fitting as possible.

steps.title: Add arterial pediatric line
steps.instruction: Use an arterial‑side pediatric blood line, cut the tubing so that 2 in remain on each side of the degassing chamber and peristaltic output, place a female 5/32 in Luer fitting into the cut tubing, and connect it to the male 3/32 in Luer fitting on the blood filter tubing.

steps.title: Prime saline through filter
steps.instruction: Open the clamp on the blood filter tubing to allow saline to flow, move the tubing until saline exits the open end, then close the clamp.

steps.title: Set up peristaltic pump
steps.instruction: Open the peristaltic pump door, place the peristaltic tubing on the left side of the pump, shape it in an inverted U around the motor, and secure it with the lower fasteners.

steps.title: Mount CytoSorb column
steps.instruction: Place the assembled CytoSorb column in a three‑pronged clamp on a ring stand, positioning the clamp at least 6 in above the stand base.

steps.title: Connect device tubing (Luer caps)
steps.instruction: If the device caps are Luer caps, place a male 5/32 in Luer fitting into the cut tubing end, connect this fitting to the device outlet, and attach the blue Luer fitting (included with the blood set) before the air filter to the device outlet.

steps.title: Connect device tubing (hose‑barb caps)
steps.instruction: If the device caps are hose‑barb caps, wrap Teflon tape around the outlet barb, place the cut tubing onto the barb, and connect the other tubing end to the inlet Luer fitting on the saline IV bag; secure the air filter in a three‑pronged clamp about 6 in above the device.

steps.title: Rotate device 180°
steps.instruction: Turn the device over 180 ° while it remains in the three‑pronged clamp.

steps.title: Connect peristaltic tubing to device (Luer)
steps.instruction: If the device caps are Luer caps, place a male 5/32 in Luer fitting into the open end of the peristaltic tubing and connect it to the device; if any saline leaked, run the pump briefly to fully prime the line before connection, then turn the device 180 ° so the outlet faces upward.

steps.title: Connect peristaltic tubing to device (hose‑barb)
steps.instruction: If the device caps are hose‑barb caps, wrap the barb with Teflon tape, place the open end of the peristaltic tubing onto the barb, run the pump briefly to prime if saline leaked, and turn the device 180 ° so the outlet faces upward.

steps.title: Open all flow clamps
steps.instruction: Open every clamp along the tubing flow route.

steps.title: Pre‑run saline recirculation
steps.instruction: Set the peristaltic pump to recirculate saline through the device at 220 mL/min for at least 3 hours before introducing blood.

steps.title: Prepare syringe for blood transfer
steps.instruction: Obtain a 140 mL syringe, remove its plunger, and set it aside.

steps.title: Make syringe tubing connector
steps.instruction: Cut ~6 in of tubing, attach a 5/32 in female Luer fitting to each end, and connect one fitting to the syringe Luer‑lock.

steps.title: Prepare reservoir IV bag
steps.instruction: Obtain a 500–2000 mL IV bag of the desired volume, cut off its bag spike, place a clamp on the cut tubing, and insert a 3/32 in male Luer fitting into the tubing end.

steps.title: Connect syringe to reservoir bag
steps.instruction: Connect the opposite end of the syringe tubing to the male Luer fitting on the IV bag and close the tubing clamp.

steps.title: Transfer blood into reservoir
steps.instruction: Obtain a filled blood bag, cut off its spike, open the clamp on the blood‑bag tubing, fill the syringe with the desired blood volume, close the blood‑bag clamp, open the clamp on the syringe tubing to allow transfer into the IV bag, then close the syringe‑tubing clamp. Repeat until the target volume is reached.

steps.title: Stop saline recirculation after blood fill
steps.instruction: After the desired blood volume is in the reservoir bag, stop the saline recirculation pump.

steps.title: Disconnect saline inlet and move filter
steps.instruction: Close the clamp on the inlet tubing of the saline IV bag, disconnect its Luer fittings, remove the blood filter from the saline reservoir, and insert it into the spike port of the blood‑reservoir bag.

steps.title: Large‑volume blood transfer – connect spikes
steps.instruction: Remove the tab covering the spike entry on the reservoir bag and insert the spike from the blood bag.

steps.title: Large‑volume blood transfer – prepare recirculation bag
steps.instruction: Cut off the spike on the recirculation IV bag, clamp the tubing, and insert a 3/32 in female Luer fitting into the open end.

steps.title: Gravity‑driven blood transfer
steps.instruction: Open the clamp to allow blood to flow from the blood bag to the reservoir bag, hang the blood bag above the recirculation bag to aid flow, and when the desired volume has transferred, remove the spike from the reservoir bag.

steps.title: Shut down saline recirculation pump
steps.instruction: Turn off the blood pump on the saline recirculation setup.

steps.title: Re‑route blood filter to blood reservoir
steps.instruction: Close the clamp on the inlet tubing of the saline reservoir, disconnect its Luer fittings, and place the blood‑filter spike into the blood‑reservoir bag.

steps.title: Prepare analyte spike syringe
steps.instruction: Obtain a 10 mL Luer‑lock syringe, remove its plunger, attach a 3/32 in female Luer cap, and use pipetters to add the desired analyte volumes (wash with 1–2 mL saline if total volume <1 mL). Replace the plunger, invert the syringe, and tap to reincorporate analyte.

steps.title: Degas and prime analyte syringe
steps.instruction: Remove the Luer cap, push the plunger up to expel air, replace the cap, then invert and tap again to recombine solution.

steps.title: Load syringe with needle
steps.instruction: Remove the Luer cap and replace it with a syringe needle.

steps.title: Add analytes to blood reservoir
steps.instruction: Pierce the membrane of the reservoir bag sample port and expel the analyte solution into the blood; while the syringe remains in the bag, draw blood into the syringe and push it back into the reservoir, repeating this three times to ensure complete mixing.

steps.title: Mix blood‑reservoir mixture
steps.instruction: If the recirculation temperature is above room temperature, place the reservoir bag on a heated water bath on an orbital shaker for 30 min; otherwise, manually tilt the bag in a clockwise rotation for at least 15 min.

steps.title: Collect T0 sample
steps.instruction: Using a 10 mL syringe with needle, draw a sample directly from the reservoir through the sample port (time 0).

steps.title: Measure hematocrit (T0)
steps.instruction: Place a heparinized capillary tube into the syringe opening, cover the top with a finger, remove the tube into sealing compound, centrifuge for 10 min at 1500×g, then measure total fluid length and red‑cell length with a ruler and record the values.

steps.title: Measure hematocrit (T300)
steps.instruction: Repeat the hematocrit measurement procedure at the 300‑minute sample point.

steps.title: Collect remaining blood sample
steps.instruction: Push the syringe plunger to transfer the remaining blood into a 5 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Prepare for blood recirculation
steps.instruction: Open all clamps along the recirculation flow path except the reservoir‑inlet clamp, disconnect the Luer‑lock fittings at the reservoir inlet, hold the device outlet tubing over a 400 mL beaker, and start the blood pump.

steps.title: Purge lines with blood/saline
steps.instruction: Purge approximately 35 mL (small), 75 mL (medium), or 150 mL (large) of blood/saline through the lines, then stop the blood pump.

steps.title: Reconnect circulation loop
steps.instruction: Reconnect the Luer fittings between the device outlet line and the reservoir inlet line.

steps.title: Start blood recirculation pump
steps.instruction: Turn the blood pump on and set the flow rate to 140 mL/min (or the required rate).

steps.title: Begin timed sampling
steps.instruction: Start a timer and collect samples at 0, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, and 300 minutes from the in‑line sampling port located before the peristaltic tubing.

steps.title: Configure centrifuge for plasma
steps.instruction: Turn on the centrifuge, verify the relative centrifugal force is set to 3000×g, temperature to 4 °C, and time to 10 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge plasma samples
steps.instruction: Immediately after each sample is placed in a collection tube, load it into the centrifuge holder and spin for 10 minutes at 3000×g.

steps.title: Label microcentrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Label two 2 mL flip‑top microcentrifuge tubes for each time point with the sample time, polymer ID, date, notebook, and page number.

steps.title: Aliquot plasma into labeled tubes
steps.instruction: Using a fresh 1 mL transfer pipet for each sample, aliquot equal volumes of plasma from the collection tube into the two labeled microcentrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Store samples
steps.instruction: Label a cardboard storage box with date, polymer ID, spiked analytes, initials, and notebook/page; place the box with all aliquoted samples into a –20 °C freezer immediately (or into a refrigerator if a freezer is unavailable, then transfer to –20 °C later).

steps.title: B12 spike experiment – prepare stock
steps.instruction: Dilute B12 in water (10 mg/mL stock) directly into bovine blood to a final concentration of 300 µg/mL.

steps.title: B12 spike experiment – recirculate blood
steps.instruction: Recirculate the spiked blood through standard tubing coupled to a 20 mL CytoSorb column at 40 mL/min for 3 hours on the benchtop.

steps.title: B12 spike experiment – plasma collection
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the blood for 10 minutes at 3000×g and collect the plasma for analysis.

steps.title: B12 spike experiment – prepare standards
steps.instruction: Prepare a standard curve using unspiked plasma and B12 stock: make a 500 µg/mL high standard (50 µL stock + 1950 µL plasma) and serially dilute to 250, 125, 62.5, 31.25, 15.625, 7.813 µg/mL plus a blank.

steps.title: B12 spike experiment – plate setup
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µL of each standard and each sample into wells of a microplate.

steps.title: B12 spike experiment – read plate
steps.instruction: Read the plate on a BioTek Gen5 microplate reader at 550 nm wavelength.
